text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- The 805 million kroon of defence expenses planned for 1998 will be 9.1 percent higher than in 1997 but by percentage in the budget it will be lower than this year, Defence Minister Andrus Oovel said.
- The police are investigating whether the man named Viktor, who threatened Norwegian retailer Varner Baltiya with bombs in its shops in Latvia, also used bombs made in a factory in Tartu.
- The Estonian Hospitals Union board warns of a crisis next year if no changes are made to the health service system.
- Russia will never turn over to Estonia the 13,500 files of KGB agents taken to Russia in 1989-1990, representatives of the Russian Federal Security Bureau told the newspaper.
- The collection of money for a Liberty Monument in central Tallinn has been a total failure, raising only 51 kroons.
- The Estonian rescue services lack equipment and existing facilities are outdated, an official said.
- The Finno-Ugric Setu chose a new king and held a peasant parade at a folk customs festival, the fourth Setu Kingdom Days in south east Estonia.
